## 1. Who is compared

**Commercial** is every Adzuna posting; **federal** is every USAJobs posting classified in scope (`jobs.in_scope`). Every figure is per market. A blended "% populated" would be a category error: federal pay bands are disclosed by law, commercial salaries by choice.

| Market | Jobs |
|---|---|
| commercial | 800 |
| federal | 50 |

## 2. Measured fields (what employers disclose)

![Grouped bars: salary present, salary disclosed, skills present, by market](measured-fields.png)

From `v_field_completeness_counts`, each rate checked against `v_field_completeness`. Commercial skills present is truncation-floored: Adzuna's ~500-character cap hides skills, so an absent tag is often a recall failure, not a skill-free posting.

| Field | Layer | Commercial | Federal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Salary | any figure present | 100.0% (800 of 800 jobs) | 100.0% (50 of 50 jobs) |
| Salary | employer-disclosed | 12.0% (96 of 800 jobs) | 100.0% (50 of 50 jobs) |
| Salary | Adzuna model estimate | 88.0% (704 of 800 jobs) | 0.0% (0 of 50 jobs) |
| Skills | ≥ 1 skill tag (any confidence) | 42.5% (340 of 800 jobs) | 98.0% (49 of 50 jobs) |
| Location | any location parsed | 100.0% (800 of 800 jobs) | 76.0% (38 of 50 jobs) |
| Company | company present | 99.9% (799 of 800 jobs) | 100.0% (50 of 50 jobs) |
| Posted date | present | 100.0% (800 of 800 jobs) | 100.0% (50 of 50 jobs) |

Salary has two layers. Adzuna returns a salary for nearly every posting, filling the gaps with its own model's estimate, so "any figure present" overstates disclosure: **employer-disclosed** is the market fact. Federal pay bands are never modelled.

## 3. Instrument-limited fields (what our classifiers can see)

These measure this project's instruments, not employer disclosure, so they are kept out of the chart and shown here with the mechanism that limits each one. Don't read them beside the measured fields.

Instrument-limited: from `v_field_completeness_counts`, checked against `v_field_completeness`.

| Field | Layer | Commercial | Federal | Why it's instrument-limited |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Seniority | title carries an explicit level | 50.0% (400 of 800 jobs) | 8.0% (4 of 50 jobs) | the classifier reads the job title only (src/cleaning/seniority.py); a level stated only in the description is invisible to it |
| Metro | in the tracked 8-city + DC list | 9.0% (72 of 800 jobs) | 22.0% (11 of 50 jobs) | a lookup against a curated allowlist (src/cleaning/metro.py), never a default; real cities outside the list count as absent. Location present is the disclosure rate |
| Remote | flagged remote | 4.0% (32 of 800 jobs) | not measurable | the classifier scans `jobs.description` only (src/cleaning/apply_cleaning.py); federal telework policy sits in `description_full`, so federal is not measurable |

## Methods and caveats

- Commercial jobs (every Adzuna posting): 800
- Federal jobs (USAJobs postings classified in scope): 50
- Never pooled across markets: every rate is one market's, with its own denominator.
- Every rate is rebuilt from `v_field_completeness_counts` and checked against the percentage `v_field_completeness` computes; a mismatch stops the report.
- Skills present counts a tag at any confidence, as `v_field_completeness` does; report 1 (commercial vs federal skills) uses confidence ≥ 0.8, so its tagged-job counts can be lower.
- Commercial skills present is **truncation-floored** (Adzuna's ~500-character cap).
- Instrument-limited fields come with their mechanism and are never charted. Federal remote is shown as "not measurable", never as a rate.
- The recon samples behind the instrument-limited labels (for example the seniority sample) are raw counts in docs/findings_field_completeness.md; they aren't in a view and aren't regenerated here.
- Sources: `sql/views/v_field_completeness.sql`, `v_field_completeness_counts.sql`; docs/phase_3_findings.md (Investigation #3); docs/findings_field_completeness.md.
